subject: Sprint 27 headroom triage — iterative reservations proposal
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Meera Shah <meera@pipelinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint 27 headroom triage — iterative reservations proposal

Team —

We ran the sprint-27 headroom model overnight (attached) and a few things jumped out that I want to triage with product/ops before we finalize next-week reservations. TL;DR: peak inference for the demo window (7/6–7/9) looks like it will exceed our committed slice by ~1.8x for the first two days, then trend down as caching warms up.

Proposal: instead of a single static carveout, we do an iterative reservation approach:
- Reserve a small baseline (30% of peak) as a committed slice for the sprint;
- Pre-authorize a 48-hour autoscale-exception window for the demo burst (explicit caps + billing guardrails);
- Post-demo reconciliation to either extend or release additional capacity after we inspect quality/latency telemetry.

Asks:
1) Kimberly — can you confirm whether finance/commitment policy allows the pre-authorize exception path for a customer demo (I flagged this with procurement but wanted core policy input)?
2) Jonas — can ops implement a 48-hour exception window with a hard token/spend cap and an automated rollback at the end of the window? What are the guardrails you need from product?
3) Laura — if we move forward, I need a crisp runbook for on-call and CS handoff (who owns alerts during the 48-hour window).

Attachments: S27_headroom_modeling.xlsx (sheets: summary, per-region sims), reservation_matrix_v2.csv (parameter grid).

I put a short matrix in the sheet for three options — baseline-reserve, iterative-reserve+burst, and full-commit — with cost estimates and latency risk. I recommend iterative-reserve+burst for the demo to preserve customer experience while minimizing committed spend.

If we agree, I'll file a formal exception and loop procurement + the external contact (Meera) to align timelines.

—David
David Kim
Head of Dedicated Capacity, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint 27 headroom triage — iterative reservations proposal

Thanks David — useful model, appreciate the detail. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I sign off:

1) Finance/commitment policy: policy permits temporary exception pre-authorizations but we need the following on the exception request: explicit start/end datetimes, a hard spend cap, and an ops-approved rollback trigger (latency or spend). So your proposal maps to policy but procurement will want the numbers filled in.

2) Billing guardrail: procurement will require a written acknowledgement from the customer for the demo burst if spend could exceed committed amounts. If we need to short-circuit that, legal sometimes accepts a signed email from the prospect.

3) SLA impact: we need to decide whether the burst lane is best-effort or SLA-backed. For demos I usually recommend best-effort with on-call monitoring — avoids permanent SLA exposure.

Next step: David — can you add the explicit start/end (UTC) and a proposed hard spend cap to the matrix? I can draft the procurement note once I have that.

- Kimberly
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Agree with the iterative approach. Operational notes and constraints:

- We can implement a 48-hour exception window and attach a spend cap; implementation requires:
  * Autoscale policy id to fork from (I'll use policy AS-std-2 for demo lanes)
  * Hard token cap enforced at the router layer (we can decline new sessions once cap hit)
  * Rollback trigger: either time-based or telemetry-based (p95 latency > 450ms for 5m).

- Risk: cold-cache during the first 6–12 hours will create a token storm. To mitigate: pre-warm critical prefixes (we can push a small synthetic traffic pattern) and set a per-customer concurrency throttle.

- Requirements from product:
  1) exact UTC start and end to configure the scheduled policy.
  2) explicit max tokens and max spend value.
  3) list of customer endpoints to whitelist for the burst (so we don't open the burst to unrelated traffic).

I linked INF-1234 in the matrix for the scheduled job. I'll draft a minimal runbook and drop it in the Drive link. If procurement needs a customer acknowledgement template, Laura — can you help with a one-line template?

—Jonas
Director, Dedicated Infrastructure

Thanks all — quick consolidation and next steps below.

Decisions:
- Path: iterative-reserve+burst (baseline reserve 30% peak, 48-hour burst window for 7/6 00:00 UTC -> 7/8 00:00 UTC).
- Spend cap: provisional hard cap set to $3,000 for the window; router will enforce a token limit equivalent.
- Scope: whitelist Pipeline Health project endpoints only.
- SLA: best-effort for the burst window; on-call to monitor p95 and trigger rollback if p95 > 450ms for 5m.

Action items:
1) Jonas to implement scheduled policy AS-std-2 fork with stated caps and pre-warm job (INF-1234) — due 7/5 EOD.
2) Laura to create the procurement acknowledgement template and publish in the Drive link — due 6/30 noon PT.
3) Kimberly to file the exception with finance/procurement once the matrix has exact UTCs and the $3,000 cap enumerated.
4) David (me) to schedule the 15-minute alignment with Meera on 6/29 10:15 PT to confirm the endpoint whitelist — joining link in Drive.

I've attached an updated reservation_matrix_v2.csv with the explicit start/end and spend cap populated. If anyone objects to the decisions above, flag in an email thread within 4 hours — otherwise I'll proceed with the formal exception filing and Ops ticket.

Thanks —
David
